HDI concerns easing
New capacity and price hikes boosting earnings visibility for 2027-28
We are increasingly confident in Gold Circuit’s transition towards higher-layer-
count HDI boards, supported by meaningful investments in technology, talent, and
new capacity. The planned capacity ramp aligns well with the next-generation

ASIC schedules of two major CSP customers, while potential layer-count increase
from 26 layers for Trainium3 to 34 layers for Trainium4 should drive meaningful
content growth. Meanwhile, PCB price hikes and improving cost pass-through
should support a sequential GM recovery from 3Q26. We raise our 2027/28 EPS
forecasts by 1%/9% and lift our TP from NT$1,955 to NT$2,000 while reiterating
our High Conviction Outperform rating.
Less concerned about the HDI transition

While the market remains concerned about Gold Circuit’s HDI capabilities, we
believe the company has recruited experienced talent and invested meaningfully in
HDI technology to support future ASIC demand. The second Thailand plant and
new capacity at the first Suzhou plant are scheduled to contribute from 2H27,
followed by the second Suzhou plant in 1H28, with all three expansions primarily
dedicated to HDI production. Importantly, the capacity ramp should align well with

the next-generation ASIC schedules of two major CSP customers. We expect Gold
Circuit to maintain its leading position in AWS Trainium4 and benefit from
meaningful content growth, driven by an increase in PCB layer count from 26 layers
for Trainium3 to 34 layers for Trainium4.
Price hikes underway
For AI accelerator PCBs, we believe Gold Circuit should gradually pass rising CCL
costs through to customers. Our checks suggest that non-AI PCB products are

being quoted at 3-4x prior price levels, with lead-times extending to at least four
months at leading PCB vendors. This indicates a tightening industry supply-demand
environment and suggests that the GM weakness seen in 2Q26 should not persist
in the coming quarters. We forecast GM to improve sequentially to 36.7%/36.8%
in 3Q26/4Q26.
Earnings revisions and valuation
We keep 2026SP EPS largely unchanged but raise our 2027/28 forecasts by 1%/9%
to reflect higher production value contributed by the new plants and increasing HDI

content. Accordingly, we raise our TP from NT$1,955 to NT$2,000, still based on
30x 2H27-1H28SP PE, and reiterate our High Conviction Outperform rating.

Investment thesis
We expect Gold Circuit to benefit from the strong CCL/PCB material upgrade trend,
rising shipments of AI servers and continued spec upgrades in CPU servers, which
require higher PCB layer counts. The upgrade in networking towards 800G should
also lead to improving margins for the company.
Catalysts
1) Accelerating server shipments driven by US CSPs and enterprise customers; 2)

server content value growth; 3) a stronger-than-expected networking demand
recovery; 4) a notebook demand recovery.
Valuation details
We value all of our coverage in the PCB/CCL space on PE as it better reflects
margins and earnings outlooks, which we believe the market will mainly focus on.
We use a target PE multiple of 30x, in line with the downstream server sector
average after the recent rerating driven by AI. Given GCE's higher-than-peer
revenue exposure to cloud servers and switches, its leading market position, and

our expectation of robust AI/ASIC server shipments with computing server demand
to gradually recover, we think 30x PE is justified as server/PC ODM suppliers have
all rerated to the 15-30x range on the back of the booming AI demand. And as GCE
also generates a similar number of sales from server and AI, it will likely enjoy strong
growth (better content growth from server and switch) and better returns (less
competition) than assemblers in the mid-to-long term.

Investment risks
Downside risks: (1) order adjustment as a result of chip shortages or supply chain
disruption; (2) weaker-than-expected cloud/datacentre Capex demand; (3) slower
adoption or delayed launch of Intel’s Eagle Stream and AMD’s Genoa platforms; (4)
further raw material price hikes, and (5) more severe competition across the
industry.

展望後市， 研究部對上銀營收表現維持正向看待 。 目前終端需求持
續暢旺，產品交期維持高位，線性滑軌能見度約 4 至 5 個月，滾
珠螺桿最長可達 6 個月 。 儘管地緣政治因素推升鋼材 、 包材與潤滑
油等原物料價格 ， 但公司具備彈性定價能力且維持多元採購策略，
漲價效益足以抵銷成本上揚。伴隨26Q3 完整反映漲價產品銷售，
預估單季營收達 80.92 億元，QoQ 7.77%，YoY 34.97%，EPS 上
看 2.81 元。放眼 2026 至 2027 年，亞洲半導體需求穩固、歐洲軍
工與航太產業接棒成為新動能 ， 整體訂單需求無虞 。 預估上銀2026
年與 2027 年營收將分別達 296.90 億元與 329.36 億元 ， 維持雙位
數年增幅，YoY 分別為 22.37%與 10.93%。在營運規模提升帶動
下，預估 2026 年、2027 年 EPS 將分別達 9.28 元與 11.87 元。 
評價方面，上銀過去五年 PER 主要集中於 20 倍至 40 倍區間。考
量公司營收與獲利將呈現雙位數成長上升趨勢，產業結構持續上
行，研究部以2027 年預估 EPS 11.87 元作為評價基礎，並給予歷
史區間中緣偏上之 35x 本益比，目標價為 420 元，給予「買進」
之投資建議。

⚫ 全球需求延續，獲利有望持續成長，估 2026 年 EPS 9.28 元 
研究部對上銀後市營收維持正向看待，係因以下：(1) 終端需
求持續暢旺，產品交期維持高位； (2) 公司具備彈性定價能
力，漲價效益足以覆蓋成本上揚；(3) 半導體產業需求穩固，
持續帶動滾珠螺桿與機器人等相關產品出貨。 
訂單能見度方面，目前整體產品交期維持高檔，線性滑軌約  
4-5 個月 ， 滾珠螺桿最長可達 6 個月 。 觀察各區域下游需求：
亞洲市場維持暢旺，其中中國受惠於電動車、電子與半導體產
業持續擴張，帶動製造設備與傳動元件需求；東南亞受惠全球
供應鏈重組，除傳統傳動元件外， 亦間接推升機器人產品需
求；台灣則持續受惠半導體與科技業資本支出，帶動螺桿與機
器人穩健成長。歐洲市場方面，儘管德國汽車工業仍顯疲態，
但軍工與航太產業已成為新成長動能，加上捷克、波蘭等中歐
製造核心需求保持穩定，有效支撐歐洲營運。

限 制，使 整 個 半 導 體 產 業 受 惠。此 轉 移 能 讓 先 進 晶 片 製 造 服 務 提 供 者 充 分 利
用 High NA EUV 的 優 勢 ， 更 提 升 未 來 世 代 先 進 晶 片 的 成 本 效 益 。 
目標於 2031 年 之 前 建 立 12 吋 光 罩 試 產 線(pilot line) ，並於 2033 年 之 前 實
現 微 影 系 統 全 面 就 緒 ， 以 支 援 先 進 製 程 量 產 。 台 積 電 並 表 示 自2030 年 起 ，
將 在 先 進 製 程 量 產 中 導 入 ASML 的 High NA 技 術 。  
12 吋光罩 使 High NA 效 率 提 升 ：  
現行 EUV 設備的 NA(Numerical Aperture ， NA) 為 0.33 ， High NA 則 提 高 到
0.55 。 NA 數 值 越 高 ， 解 析 度 也 越 高 、 曝 光 時 能 呈 現 的 細 節 愈 多 。ASML 資

8 奈 米 ， 也 就 是 能 在 晶 圓 上 印 出 更 細 微 的 電 路 圖 形 。 部 分 原 本 需 要2 次 甚 至
更多次曝光才能完成的圖形，也有機會改以單次曝光處理，降低製程複雜
度 、 缺 陷 風 險 與 生 產 周 期 。

A14 、 A10 金 屬 層 圖 形 ；High NA EUV ， 只 要 1 張 光 罩 就 能 完 成 相 同 圖 形 。
但 解 析 度 提 高 ，High NA 的 光 學 設 計 讓 單 次 可 曝 光 範 圍 縮 小 到 原 本EUV 的

三. 台光電低軌道衛星板材， 2027 年隨發射進程量增  
台光電於 低 軌 道 衛 星 延 伸 的 商 機，回顧 2025 年 低 軌 衛 星 發 射 量 增
加至 3~3.5 萬顆 (Space X 與 Amazon LEO 發 射 量 ， 年 增 率 達
+45%YoY) ，台 光 電、華 通 等 廠 商 投 入 資 源 開 發 低 軌 道 衛 星PCB 板
材，可 望 受 惠 低 軌 衛 星 鋪 設 建 置 量 增。宏 遠 投 顧 觀 察，低 軌 衛 星 量
體 近年來 成 長 快 速 ，2027 年以前， S 客 戶 進 入 火 箭V2mini 轉換至
V3 版 本 切 換 期(4Q26 開 始 重 啟 新 版 本)，Amazon LEO 發 射 時 程預
計 2027 年 以 前 發 射 量1,500~1,600 顆、 2029 年 發 射 量 達3,200 顆，
長 期 低 軌 衛 星 仍 呈 現 成 長 。天上衛星 PCB 板 技 術 層 次 高 台 光 電 、
華通的市佔率高 )， 天 上 衛 星 PCB 板與相對應之地面接收站量增
長，帶動 2025 ~2027 年 低 軌 衛 星 產 能 足 以 支 應增加 +40~ 50%YoY 拉
貨動能 。低 軌 大 型S 客戶 V3 版 本 新 型 火 箭 搭 載 低 軌 衛 星，所 採 用
之 銅 箔 基 板 升 級 至M8 等 級，材 料 損 耗 要 求 降 低，訊 號 傳 出 完 整 性
標 準 提 高 ， 對 於CCL 、PCB(HDI) 、 玻 纖 與 銅 箔 等 規 格 預 期 同 步 升
級 ， 推 升 材 料 成 本 與PCB 產值。

四.預估 2026/2027 年稅後 EPS 120.77/204.85 元 
2026 年受惠 AI 伺 服 器及 ASIC 需 求 持 續 強 勁 的 帶 動 下 ， 台 光 電 為
銅 箔 基 板 領 導 廠 商 ， 將 受 惠AI Server 對 於 高 階 銅 箔 基 板強 勁 的 需
求 ， 因 而，預估 2026 年 台 光 電 營 收 為1,999.92 億 元 ，+112.17%YoY ，
毛利率 34.21% ，稅 後 淨 利 432.76 億 元，稅 後 EPS+120.77 元。展 望
2027 年，在 AI 伺服器 需 求 持 續 強 勁 的 帶 動 下 ， 帶 動 產 能 持 續 增
長， 預估 2027 年 台 光 電 營 收 為3,530.14 億 元，+76.57%YoY ，毛 利
率為 35.49% ， 稅 後 淨 利734.03 億 元 ， 稅 後EPS+204.85 元。

四.投資建議維持 買進，目標價 6,145 元 
宏 遠 投 顧 認 為，台 光 電營 運 重 點 在 於，營 運 動 能 於2026 年 起 加 速
啟 動，一 般 型 伺 服 器CPU 廠商 Intel 、AMD 均 有 新 品 帶 動 新 平 台 升
級 與 相 關 供 應 的 零 組 件 商 機，以 及 攻 入AI 伺 服 器、高 階 網 路 交 換
器的 CCL 、 低 軌 衛 星CCL 規 格 轉 換 成 長 可 期。 基 於 上 述 ， 給 予台
光電 投 資 建 議 為 買 進 ， 目 標 價6,145 元(30.00x 20 27 EPS) 。

盟立 (2464 TT)

重新覆蓋  
買進(Buy) 
產能擴張推升 2027 成長，機器人接棒第二曲線  
⚫ 在手訂單充沛， 2027 營收成長能見度高  
⚫ 半導體需求強勁 ，產能同步擴張  
⚫ 機器人由小量走向量產，長期成長空間可期  
在手訂單充沛， 2027 營收成長能見度高 ：盟立 2025 年營收 66.81 億
元，毛利率 18.8% ，EPS -0.8 元，近年持續投入新客戶 與 新 專 案 開 發，
為後續擴產需求預作布局。進入 2026 年後營運逐步轉強， 2Q26 營收
21.69 億元 (QoQ +16% 、YoY +7.9%)， 毛利率 22.2%，EPS 0.42 元，1H26
轉虧為盈，主要受惠先進封裝擴產，帶動 OHT、AGV 及 Stocker 等產
品成長。截至 8 月累計接單約 140 億元，其中半導體占 75% 、智能物
流 10%~15% ，年底訂單有望接近 200 億元，且 75%~80% 可望於 2027
年底前完成， 預期今年營收呈現逐月、逐季提升趨勢 。 
半導體需求強勁，產能同步擴張 ：半導體仍是盟立未來最重要的成長
核心，公司目前聚焦先進封裝、高階載板及半導體自動化三大領域，
部分客戶擴產規劃已延伸至 2028~2029 年，部分載板客戶既有擴產仍
不足以滿足需求，持續尋找新廠房與土地。此外， 公司產品技術已具
備進入 Fab 的條件 ，若後續能成功由 OSAT 及先進封裝延伸至前段
Fab ，單一客戶需求量與設備價值將進一步放大。 產品面， 2027 年底
OHT 產能目標 2,500~3,000 台，對應月產能約 250 台，較先前月產能
100 台大幅成長 ；EFEM 產能目標 3,000 台，Stocker 500~800 台，AMR 
800~1,000 台， 整體 產能 規模 將明顯 放大 。 海外 市場 也是為 下一 階段
成長動能，目前有 9.3 億元訂單於海外執行。  
機器人由小量走向量產，長期成長空間可期 ：機器人方面，盟英進度
持續 推進， 目前北美客戶已開始小量出貨，年底諧波減速機產能目標
30 萬顆以上， 2027 年有望進一步提升至 80 萬顆。現階段仍處於量產
初期，固定成本、折舊與設備投入較高，產量需達到數十萬顆以上規
模才較容易跨過損平點。機器人 2026 年仍偏向小量貢獻， 2027 年開
始觀察損平與放量進度， 2028 年後 將成為第二成長曲線。 我們預估 盟
立 2026/2027 年營收達 98.5 /146.7 億元、EPS  2.51 /6.8 元，給予 「買進」
評等，目標價 238 元(2027 年 EPSx 35 倍)。 
風險因子： 半導體客戶擴產遞延 、機器人產品競爭加劇 。

盟立成立於 1989 年，為台灣主要自動化 系統整合廠商之一，營運模式以「系
統整合 (SI)+ 自 有設 備 」為 核 心 ， 業務 涵 蓋半 導體 、 面 板 、物 流 及機 器人 等 領
域。近年公司策略明顯聚焦半導體自動化市場，主要產品包括空中走行式搬
送系統 (OHT) 、晶圓 /載 板 傳 送 設 備(EFEM) 、 晶 圓 儲 存 設 備(Stocker) 及 無 人 搬
運車 (AMR/AGV) 。 
生產據點方面，公司目前於竹科、銅鑼、中科及南科均設有生產基地，其中
竹科以機器人相關產品為主，銅鑼及南科負責 OHT ，中科則生產 Stocker 及
EFEM 。隨半導體客戶持續擴廠，公司近年積極進行產品規格標準化及生產流
程優化，包括 OHT 機種收斂、軌道規格統一，以及軟體平台模組化，有利後
續由專案型生產逐步轉向標準化、規模化製造，降低單位生產成本並提升交
付效率。我們認為，盟立在半導體自動化市場的核心競爭優勢，在於產品線
完整及軟硬體整合能力 。半導體廠內 OHT、EFEM、Stocker 及 AMR 之間需高
度整合，設備導入後具一定系統黏著度，其中 OHT、EFEM 與 AMR 等設備在
資訊串聯及搬運指令整合上具有較高連動性，有利盟立由單一設備進一步擴
大整體專案供應範圍。  
除半導體設備外，公司也積極布局機器人產業。旗下盟英科技主要投入諧波
減速機及關節模組，並透過 傲威科技向整機機器人領域延伸。 2026 年公司與
精確、敏實集團合資成立傲威科技，由盟立提供技術與產品、敏實集團負責
結構件，進一步強化機器人整機整合能力。  
圖表一、盟立產能配置

資料來源：盟立，中信投顧整理  
AI 伺服器、 HPC 及先進封裝需求持續成長，使全球半導體資本支出進入新一
輪擴張週期。本輪擴產範圍涵蓋晶圓代工、記憶體、先進封裝、封測及載板
等領域，同步帶動廠內自動化搬運設備需求。  
台積電 ，2026 年 Capex 已上修至 600 ～640 億美元 ，公司更宣布額外投資 1,000
億美元用以在美新建 4 座新廠 ；也規劃台灣未來數年將興建高達 13 座先進製
程及先進封裝廠房 。我們預估台積電 2026/2027/2028 年全球合計在建案量分
別達 16/16/5 座， 2026~2028 年 Capex 合計突破 2,000 億美元。

圖表二、 台積電各廠區興建時程表

封測產業進入擴產週期，受惠 AI 需求強勁及台積電先進封裝產能快速擴張，
部分後段封裝製程委外至 OSAT 廠，日月光、京元電、力成、矽格及南茂等
業者擴產規劃積極 。 對盟立而言 ， 封測與先進封裝產能擴張將同步帶動 OHT 、
Stocker 、AMR 等自動化搬運設備需求。  
目前盟立 OHT 於 OSAT 端已完成部分客戶認證並進入接單及專案執行階段；
前端 FAB 市場則持續推進驗證與導入 。 Stocker 已通過晶圓廠客戶驗證 ， EFEM
則受惠高階 ABF 載板客戶擴產需求，相關載板客戶建廠規劃已延伸至 2029
年。  
圖表 三、OSAT 廠擴廠進度整理

資料來源：各公司，中信投顧整理  
人形機器人目前仍處於由技術驗證走向量產的初期階段。人形機器人市場規
模 2025~2030 年 CAGR  47.1% ，2030 年市場規模估達 390 億美元，顯示中長
期產業具高度成長潛力。在人形機器人關鍵零組件中，諧波減速機主要應用
於機器人關節系統。單台人形機器人使用約 15~18 顆諧波減速機；新一代機
種可能增加至 20 餘顆。

### Page 1

Taiwan Information Technology

What’s new: We provide our update on Aspeed following its upbeat 4Q26 
revenue guidance on 4 September. We believe the strong guidance 
reaffirms our positive view that agentic AI has served as a catalyst for end 
demand for regular servers starting early 2026. Baseboard management 
controller (BMC) shipments for general servers (AI and non-AI together) 
should grow c.50% YoY in 2026. We believe that the new 4Q26 revenue 
guidance implies regular server shipment volume will increase c.50% YoY 
in 2027, hence the 36/34% uplift in our 2027/28E earnings forecasts.

What’s the impact: Solid regular server shipments ahead. Aspeed’s 
latest guidance range for its 4Q26 sales at TWD6.6-6.8bn implies 4Q26 
BMC shipments of c.12m. With this run-rate, total BMC shipments in 2027 
should be near c.50m, much higher than our previous estimate of 36.1m. 
We attribute the ongoing strength to agentic AI and AI-related general-
purpose demand. We forecast Aspeed’s BMC for general servers to 
increase to 27m in 2027E (from 18m in 2026E and 13m in 2025). At the 
same time, we expect BMC for AI servers to increase c.50% to 20m in 
2027E (up from 13m in 2026E and 5m in 2025). To sum up, we now 
forecast BMC shipments of 32.7m in 2026 and 47.6m in 2027 (+46% YoY 
in 2027). Based on our AI-related general server assumptions (excluding 
non-AI general servers), we expect the CPU:XPU ratio to rise to 1:1.3 in 
2027E (from 1:2.6 in 2026E). We expect a rising CPU:XPU ratio to become 
a key growth driver and share-price catalyst in the years after 2027. Due to 
the solid end demand, management is considering adjusting its pricing 
again from November to factor in the additional packaging cost, leading to 
our higher gross margin assumptions from 4Q26.

New growth opportunities. Following our visits to Aspeed’s booth at 
Computex 2026 and the OCP APAC conference, we believe Aspeed will 
continually maximise the dollar content per server board. Compared with 
last year’s version (embedded software-defined FPGA), Aspeed is 
integrating a Lattice FPGA into its next-generation Bridge IC (SMC; 
AST1840), which should support higher ASPs for its products.

What we recommend: We lift our 2026-28E EPS by 9-36% to factor in our 
higher BMC shipment assumptions. We lift our 12M TP to TWD26,660 
(from TWD19,800), based on an unchanged PER of 66x (high end of its 
past-3-year PER range of 21-78x), applied to our 1-year forward EPS 
forecast. Our 2025-28E EPS CAGR of 83% makes our target PER 
undemanding, given the resulting PEG ratio of 0.8. Key downside risk: 
weak AI server demand.

How we differ: Our 2026-28E EPS are 6-26% higher than the consensus, 
likely due to our bullish view on Aspeed’s ASP and shipment story.

14 September 2026

Promising outlook on agentic AI

➢ Rising CPU:XPU ratio is becoming a key growth driver for Aspeed… 
➢ … which indicates solid regular server demand despite supply hiccups 
➢ Reaffirming our Buy (1) rating and raising 12-month TP to TWD26,660

Company profile 
Established in November 2004, Aspeed is a fabless IC design company specialising in baseboard 
management controllers (BMCs), which are mostly used for the remote management of servers. Aspeed 
is a global leader in BMC, with about 70% market share. Its other products include PC/AV extension 
SoC, which supports the extension of digital signals of PCs or multimedia content to remote terminals; 
and Cupola360, which is a spherical image processor that supports 360-degree cameras.

### Page 5

5

ASPEED Technology (5274 TT): 14 September 2026 
ESG analysis

Update Date: 14 Sep 2026 
Source: Daiwa, Company

ESG risks
Risks Management Analyst comments
G
Executive/board
quality 2
Aspeed’sboard consists of 9 directors, with 4 independent directors. The directors’backgrounds
appear to have a high correlation to semiconductors (either education or work experience),
which we see as a positive for executive quality. In 2025, Aspeed held 6 board meetings and the
average attendee rate was 100%. Given Aspeed’sChairman is also the CEO, we think it is a
negative factor for board/executive management as well as external shareholders.
Capital management 1
Aspeed declared a DPS of TWD80 in 2025, representing an 77% payout ratio. Being a leading
global board management controller (BMC) IC design vendor with c.70% market share globally,
the company’sleading position and asset-light model (major expenses are from R&D
employees) allow it to maintain high ROE/ROA ratios and a high dividend payout policy. BMC IC
recently penetrated new applications (such as power supply, storage, edge servers), which can
improve its profitability on a higher revenue scale, in our view.
Related party &
transaction 2
In 2025, there were no sales to or purchases from related parties. In previous years, the main
purchases from related parties was from Avago. After selling its fully-owned Emulex unit to
Aspeed, Avago (Broadcom) became an Aspeed's shareholder with a c.6% stake in 2016. We
believe the bargaining power from its 6% shareholding was not sufficient to preload its IC
products on Aspeed's products or earn unfair profits. In any case, this relationship ended in
February 2021. As such, we see limited risk from related-party transactions.
S Supply chain
management 1
Aspeed ensures that suppliers comply with social responsibility, green environmental protection,
occupational safety and health, human rights and RBA, and prefer to work with ISO9001,
ISO14001 and ISO45001 certified suppliers. In addition, every Aspeed supplier is required to
issue a publicly disclosed sustainability management report.
E Water & wastewater
management 1
Being a fabless IC design company, Aspeed’sbusiness doesn’tinvolve a production process.
According to the company's data, it produced 4,035 tonnes of wastewater in 2025. As such, we
see limited risk from its water and waste water management.
E
Waste & hazardous
materials
management
1
Being a fabless IC design company, Aspeed’sbusiness doesn’tinvolve production processes
that may produce hazardous materials. That said, the company indicated it would employ green
design concepts and simplified product structures throughout its R&D process in order to reduce
pollution. As such, we see limited risk from its waste and hazardous materials management.
E GHG emissions 1
Due to its fabless business model, Aspeed produces limited emissions of GHG, wastewater, and
waste materials each year. According to the company’sdata, it produced around 273.5 tonnes of
CO2 in 2025.

Co-Tech Development Corp.  | Asia Pacific
Southeast Asia expansion points
to longer-term capacity upside
What’s new? Co-Tech’s board approved the establishment of a subsidiary in
Southeast Asia.
Our view: We expect the facility to primarily produce RG-series (advanced RTF)
copper foil, mainly used in general servers, switches or LEO satellites. Volume
production could begin in 2H28, with monthly capacity exceeding 500 tons. We
currently model Co-Tech’s RG-series capacity at 1,000 tons by end-2026 and 1,200

tons by end-2027. The Southeast Asia expansion therefore implies upside to our
current capacity assumptions, assuming all else remains unchanged, with
contribution likely starting in 2H28. We also believe adding RG-series capacity in
Southeast Asia could free up existing Taiwan capacity for higher-end HVLP4+ copper
foil production. Stay OW.

### Page 1

EQUITY: OSAT
Chipbond Technology Corporation   6147.TWO 6147 TT
Global Markets Research
14 September 2026
Concrete improvement in fundamentals in sight
Solid SiPh demand and future opportunities; baseline 
business benefiting from AI ripple effect; upgrade to Buy
Upgrade to Buy on increased progress in SiPh and potential DDIC backend reshuffles, 
with a new TP of TWD270, implying 43% upside
We were encouraged by Chipbond’s efforts to utilize its idle bumping capacity and make inroads 
into silicon photonics (SiPh) but did not upgrade the stock as we assumed that the market has 
likely priced in much more than it would deliver (report). Beside the reset in the market sentiment 
(share price -38% from the peak in late May vs. TAIEX +3%), we see increased progress in 
Chipbond’s bumping services in SiPh and that its baseline DDIC business could enjoy the “AI 
ripple effect” given a Korean DDIC vendor’s supply chain reshuffle. We lift our 2026/27/28F EPS 
from TWD4.55/5.71/ 6.70 to TWD5.77/9.04/10.60 (Fig. 2) . We upgrade Chipbond to Buy from 
Neutral and raise TP to TWD270 (from TWD171), which is based on 30x (unchanged)  2027F 
EPS of TWD9.04, at the high end of the company’s historical band (Fig. 4) to capture the 
diversification into SiPh. Chipbond currently trades at 21x 2027F EPS. Downside risks are softer-
than-expected optical communication demand and slower new project ramp-up.
TIA bumping remains the major driver in SiPh; TFLN engagement worth watching
While the addressable segments of Chipbond’s gold bumping include transimpedance amplifier 
(TIA), photodetector (PD), driver and modulator, we believe so far only TIA and PD are in 
production, and most of Chipbond’s SiPh revenue comes from 200G TIA bumping due to a 
larger die size than PD, with tie-ups with most of the major North American vendors. We estimate 
Chipbond’s SiPh revenue to grow 110%/70% in 2027-28F and contribute low-/high-teens of 
revenue vs. c.6% in 2026F; thus, a more significant mix benefit could support GM growth to 
32.7%/34.4% in 2027-28F from 29.4% in 2026F. Additionally, we believe Chipbond’s backend 
collaboration with UMC (2303 TT, Buy) in thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) modulator production is 
worth watching given a much larger die size.
Share gain in LDDI backend might mitigate some device unit pressure
We expect Chipbond’s revenue growth to moderate in 4Q26F after +14% q-q growth in 3Q26F on a 
N American handset brand’s seasonal demand and SiPh resilience given continued PC/ Android 
demand headwinds to Chipbond’s baseline DDIC business (~80% of current revenue). However, 
we noted before that a Korea DDIC vendor could engage with UMC due to the company’s captive 
fab partner’s likely 8” capacity offloading amidst resource constraints  (report). The capacity 
optimization might cover more than fabrication but also gold bumping, and we think Chipbond could 
thus have the opportunity to gain LDDI backend share from 2027F in the earliest.

### Page 3

Company profile
Chipbond is one of the world's leading DDI OSAT players. Established in 1997, Chipbond specialises in providing display driver and radio-frequency
semiconductor packaging and testing services.
Valuation Methodology
Our TP of TWD270 is based on 30x 2027F EPS. Our target P/E of 30x is at the high end of the historical P/E range. TAIEX is the benchmark index.
Risks that may impede the achievement of the target price
Downside risks: 1) Softer-than-expected silicon photonic demand or fiercer competition, 2) slower-than-expected smartphone and TV demand, 3)

weaker-than-expected COF/tape demand.
ESG
Chipbond manages its corporate social responsibility by focusing on five dimensions: corporate governance, workplace of well-being, environmental
and sustainable development, customer service and supplier management, and social participation. The company sets water-saving milestones and
establishes low-carbon plants in practice.

Definition of Nomura Group's equity research rating system and sectors
The rating system is a relative system, indicating expected performance against a specific benchmark identified for each individual stock, 
subject to limited management discretion. An analyst’s target price is an assessment of the current intrinsic fair value of the stock based on an 
appropriate valuation methodology determined by the analyst. Valuation methodologies include, but are not limited to, discounted cash flow 
analysis, expected return on equity and multiple analysis. Analysts may also indicate expected absolute upside/downside relative to the stated 
target price, defined as (target price - current price)/current price.

SECTORS
A 'Bullish' stance, indicates that the analyst expects the sector to outperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Neutral' stance, 
indicates that the analyst expects the sector to perform in line with the Benchmark during the next 12 months. A 'Bearish' stance, indicates that 
the analyst expects the sector to underperform the Benchmark during the next 12 months. Sectors that are labelled as 'Not rated' or shown as

Global Research
First Read
Advantech
UBS Taiwan Summit 2026 key takeaways: Four
growth engines to drive robust orders
Upbeat FY26 outlook reinforced
Advantech delivered a positive message at the UBS 2026 Taiwan Summit, backed by an
upward-trending monthly book-to-bill (BB) ratio and accumulating design win projects
in its major market in the US. The company continues to see solid order placement, not
impacted by higher pricing. Advantech's component sourcing further improved QoQ to

support robust order momentum. On profitability, Advantech can pass on over 70% of
component cost increases. Despite positive operating leverage, management noted
possibly higher opex due to restricted stock award (RSA) expenses, which have relatively
higher amortization during the first few years, starting in 2027.
Leading indicators support robust order growth
Advantech's sustained order momentum is not impacted by higher pricing, with no
signs of client double booking. Some clients even offer 100% down-payments seeking

Advantech's on-time delivery. Management sees an upward trending BB ratio, healthy
at less than 2x.  Pipeline visibility is further reinforced by North American design wins of
US$444m in H126. Orders are mainly supported by three major end applications: 1)
factory automation (particularly AMRs and cobots), semi equipment (front- and back-
end equipment), 2) healthcare, 3) green energy infrastructure.   Management expects
those and edge AI projects to be the major  order drivers in the next three to five years.

Margin pressure to ease as component headwinds subside
Advantech’s GM fell to 37.7% in Q226 due to escalating component costs, particularly
across tech inputs such as GPUs, CPUs, MLCCs, memory and PCBs. After initial price
hikes in Oct 2025, Advantech has maintained bi-weekly price adjustments for board
products and monthly adjustments for systems in 2026, allowing it to pass on over 70%
of cost increases. To mitigate supply constraints, Advantech has signed LTAs and

qualified more alternative component suppliers. It has also worked through specialized
PCB bottlenecks. Its supply sufficiency has further improved in Q326 vs. Q226.
Management maintained  guidance of flat QoQ GM and OPM for Q326, while remaining
confident the long-term GM will recover to its historical 39–40% range and OPM will
continue to trend upward, driven by expanding operating leverage.
Valuation: Raise price target to NT$782; maintain Buy

We raise our 2026-28E earnings, mainly to reflect: 1) stronger-than-expected top-line
growth; 2) lower GM on continued input cost pressure and time lags for price increases
to be reflected in its P&L; and 3) possibly higher opex starting in 2027 on RSA expense
amortization. The RSA was  approved by the board but not yet issued, pending
regulatory authority approval. We raise our price target from NT$744 to NT$782 and
reiterate our Buy rating on the solid top-line momentum.

Company Description
Established in 1981 and listed on the Taiex in 1999, Advantech is a world-leading Taiwanese
IPC supplier. Its product offerings involve embedded boards and chassis, industrial computers
and controls, and after-sales services with applications spanning manufacturing automation,

healthcare, transportation, energy and networking industries. To serve the global market, it
has three manufacturing sites in Taiwan, Japan and China and direct subsidiaries in 27
countries.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We base our price target for Advantech on 30x 2027E PE.
Industrial PC sector risks include: slower global economic growth; uncertain trade tariff
negotiations; higher interest rates that could result in weaker capex investment; readiness

and supply chain bottlenecks of IT technology that could slow project execution; currency
movement; and changes in component pricing that could bring downside to profitability.
In our view, key company-specific risks include: 1) slower-than-expected edge-AI product
adoption; 2) competition in the non-AI IPC segment, especially in China; 3) rising component
prices; 4) NTD appreciation against the USD; 5) slower macroeconomic growth that could
negatively impact overall capex allocation; and 6) demand growth that could attract more

new suppliers to join the market, which may intensify competition and possibly bring price
pressure.

Global Research
First Read
Global Unichip
2026 Taiwan Summit:  CPU momentum and
ADAS projects support 2027F outlook
FY26 revenue outlook revised higher on improved wafer support
GUC attended our 2026 Taiwan Summit on Sep 14th. August revenue of NT$5,840mn
(+1%MoM/+111%YoY) is tracking above at 73%/75% of UBSe/Street +15%/+11%
QoQ. Following better-than-expected wafer support from TSMC, management raised its
FY26 revenue growth guidance from 36% YoY to approximately 100% in late-July, with

turnkey revenue expected to grow by over 100% and NRE revenue by high teens %.
Management maintained its 2026 corporate GM target of 20%+, despite rising revenue
contribution from its top  CPU customer. OPEX is expected to increase by high teens %
YoY, due to the new Turing center and higher employee bonuses, but strong revenue
growth should still drive meaningful operating leverage.
CPU project supports near-term growth and deepen CSP engagement

CPU turnkey project for the top CSP remains the main growth driver in H226F,
supported by increased wafer allocations for both the CPU project and GUC’s other top
customers. While the current CPU project carries a relatively lower margin given leading
CSP's extensive in-house design efforts, it has also strengthened GUC's customer
relationships. This has helped it secure the next-generation dual-die  CPU project, which
carries higher content and ASP and  should see initial revenue from late-2026 with more

significant revenue contribution in 2027E. GUC is also pursuing ASIC  accelerator
opportunities with the top CSP customer and the other major CSPs, although
management does not expect meaningful turnkey revenue before 2028.
Broader customer exposure supports medium-term growth
Beyond the current CPU ramp, GUC sees incremental growth opportunities across
ADAS, other CSP CPU/ASIC business, and CPO. Chinese customers'  ADAS turnkey
revenue is expected to begin in late 2026F, followed by a its U.S. 3nm ADAS project in

H227F, with both carrying higher margins than the current CPU program, although the
U.S. customer's ramp will depend on TSMC's capacity support. For the other CSP
customer, management expects revenue contribution from both CPU and ASIC   to begin
in H226F and could become another key  revenue driver in 2027. It is also working with
this CSP customer for Gen 3 and bidding on Gen 4 project. Although  CPO remains at an
early stage, GUC and its partners plan for  tape out  on TSMC’s COUPE by end-2026,

offering longer-term margin support given GUC’s greater involvement in chip design.
Valuation: Maintain Buy rating with a P/E-based price target of NT$6,700
We rate GUC BUY with a PT of  NT$6,700, based on 50x average 2027-28E EPS (vs
historical 15-62x range), supported by 52% CAGR in earnings over 2025-30E. We
reiterate that GUC should benefit from Google CPU upside and multiple automotive
project ramps.

Company Description
Global Unichip (GUC) is a leading IC design service company in Taiwan, founded in 1998. The
company's business is to design chipsets for customers that do not have IC design capability,
with the goal of reducing entry barriers and risks for chipset design and shortening the time

to market. The company's target to enable more IC design for start-ups and system
companies is complimentary with TSMC, which would benefit from a growing customer and
application base, in addition to the company's existing IC design and IDM customers.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We value Global Unichip based on a PE methodology.
Downside risks include a slower-than-expected business recovery for mature node, lack of
new project wins, and wafer capacity constraints.

### Page 1

Poya  (5904.TWO)
Positives Mostly Priced In; Downgrade to Neutral 
CITI'S TAKE 
We downgrade Poya to Neutral from Buy following its strong YTD share price 
performance. Although operating momentum remains positive in the near-
term (we expect a strong Sep SSSG and solid 3Q earnings), we believe the 
rally has already reflected much of the benefit from robust SSSG YTD and 
margin expansion. Looking ahead, tough comparisons from 4Q26E may 
make solid SSSG harder to sustain, limiting earnings upside and potential 
weighing on stock sentiment. Meanwhile, Cosmed’s expanding rollout of 
Olive Young brands adds to competition pressure for beauty spending. We 
trim our DCF-based TP to NT$70, implying 18x NTM P/E vs. 5-year mean of 
17x. We view current risk/reward as balanced. 
Strong performance leaves less room for further upside — Poya’s shares have 
rallied 73% YTD, outperforming the benchmark’s 57% gain and broadly flat 
performance for the TW retail sector. This reflects strong operating deliver, including 
6-7% YTD SSSG and solid margin expansion supported by op leverage and 
headcount optimization. While the company may continue to grow earnings through 
store expansion and productivity improvements, we believe much of this outlook is 
already priced in. Further share price appreciation may require additional earnings 
upside, which could become more difficult to deliver if SSSG moderates. 
Tougher comp from 4Q26E could temper SSSG momentum — Poya’s YTD SSSG 
has benefited from 4-5% ticket growth, partly reflecting price inflation, as well as 
traffic growth 1-2%. We expect the comp base to become more demanding from 
4Q26E onward, increasing the hurdle for keeping the current growth rate. Slower 
SSSG could reduce incremental op leverage and limit further margin expansion. 
Given its YTD rally, a shift to positive but slower growth could weigh on sentiment. 
Cosmed’s Olive Young rollout raises competition pressure — Cosmed introduced 
four Olive Young, Korea’s leading beauty retail channel, proprietary brands in late 
Dec 2025 and planned to expand dedicated sections to 120 stores by end-2026E 
( ~20% of Cosmed’s total store count), increasing local access to popular Korean 
beauty products. Per Cosmed, PSD at locations carrying OY brands increased by 
MSD y/y YTD vs. MSD y/y down across its overall network, suggesting the brands are 
gaining customer interest. We believe broader availability and product selection 
could intensity competition for customer visits and beauty spending, potentially 
slowing Poya’s traffic growth and increasing promotional pressure.  (continued)

Poya (5904.TWO): Positives Mostly Priced In;
Downgrade to Neutral
Implications — We keep our earnings estimates largely unchanged for 2026-
2028E yet we trim our DCF-based TP to NT$70 from prior NT$74.5 mainly to factor
in a lower terminal growth of 4.5% (down from 5%). We also factor in its stock split
in Aug 2026. Our target price of NT$70 implies an 18x NTM forward P/E vs its 5-
year historical mean of 17x, which looks balanced to us.

We believe Poya’s store expansion and efficiency improvements may continue to
support earnings, but we see limited scope for further re-rating given the earnings
growth moderation (net profits +9% y/y in 2027E vs. +27% y/y in 2026E based on
our estimate) and its strong share-price gains to date. T ougher comparisons and
rising competition add uncertainty around the durability of SSSG momentum and
margin expansion.
We would prefer to see sustained traffic growth through the higher comp base,

clearer evidence of additional earnings upside or a more attractive entry point
before becoming more positive on the shares.

Poya
Company description
Poya is the largest retailer of fast-moving consumer goods in Taiwan, focusing
on low-priced cosmetics, accessories, clothing and food products for females
aged 15-49. Poya had 470 stores in Taiwan at the end of 2025 and believes
that the market can accommodate up to 700-800 stores before reaching
saturation.
Investment strategy
We have a Neutral rating on Poya. We think YTD rally has baked in most

positives, including strong SSSG and solid margin expansion. While
fundamentals remain solid, tougher comparisons from 4Q26E could
moderate this year's 6-7% SSSG, lowering operating leverage and capping
further earnings upside. Meanwhile, Cosmed's expanding rollout of Olive
Young brands is intensifying competition for beauty spending. Although
Poya's SSSG has remained resilient, braoder distribution of these brands
could divert customer traffic and increase promotional pressure. We continue

to recognize Poya's execution in store expansion and ongoing efficiency
improvements. However, with these strengths largely reflected in the share
price and growth momentum facing a higher hurdle from 4Q26E onward, we
see a more balanced risk/reward.
Valuation
We derive our 12-month target price of NT$70 for Poya from a DCF valuation
method. Our assumptions include a terminal growth rate of 4.5% and WACC
of 10.1% (beta of 1.05; risk-free rate of 4%; risk premium of 7.0%; cost of equity

of 11.3%). Our target price implies a P/E of 18x on our NTM EPS.
Risks
Key downside risks that could mean the shares fail to achieve our target price
include: intense price competition among online retailers, slower store traffic,
margin dilution due to aggressive store expansion, and a soft macro
environment.
Key upside risks that could mean the shares fail to achieve our target price
include: easing price competition among online retailers, stronger store

traffic, margin expansion thanks to strong cost control, and a stronger macro
environment.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

ab 18 September 2026
Global Research
First Read
Wiwynn
Reaffirm the strong   growth through 2027
New platforms support AI strength into 2027 while general server slower
before next ramp in 2027
We maintain our Buy on Wiwynn with a price target of $ 2,470  and also in the
UBS regional most preferred tech list. Amid the market noise, we stay positive on the
company's growth, with catalysts from liquid cooled ASIC servers in initial production
and ramping up further through 2027 and Helios racks on track as a new project

commencing from late 2026E through 2027. We do see general server cooling into Sep
and Q426 to offset the ASIC server ramp before picking up from Q127 as customers
transition to the next-generation Clearwater Forest/Venice platforms.
August sales ahead supported by general server growth
Wiwynn August sales of NT$144.3bn, +22.6% MoM, 50.4% YoY tracked ahead at
74%/73% UBSe/Street of +27%/+29% QoQ estimate in Q3. We believe the growth is
driven mainly driven by pre-build ahead of further price hikes. The company is seeing

tight supply across major component includes memory, CPU and PCB, but the impact on
deliveries has been limited through August. Since Q226, the company has booked
general server memory on its balance sheet rather than through sales and COGs, which
lifted gross margin in Q2. We factor in lower NRE and mix shifting from general server
now the highest margin with the consigned memory toward ASIC to lower GM/OpM off
the higher Q2 base of 9.3/7.3% to 8.8/6.8% in Q3 and 8.7/6.7% in Q4.

Multiple drivers support another strong year in 2027
We maintain 2027 revenue growth +89% YoY to NT$2,491bn, reflecting strength
across ASICs further ramping and rising liquid penetration toward 30% this generation,
GPUs with Helios racks ramping to 6-7k and general server continuing double digit
volume growth. We keep more conservative on Vera Rubin following limited shipments
on GB300 although should begin shipping in small volumes in Q426 and contributing

~2% of sales in 2027.
Reiterate our BUY with  price target of NT$2,470 (7,350 pre-split)
Following the recent 3-1 stock split, all per-share data below are on a post-split basis. We
reiterate our Buy rating and keep our basic EPS of NT$226.4/NT$174.1 reflecting better
margins, intact ASIC and general server ramps and customer AMD project from Q4 into
2027. Our PT of NT$2,470 is based on same 14x P/E on 2027E EPS also with 3% cash
yield (NT$74 cash dividend). We maintain a positive view reflecting Wiwynn's leverage

to ASIC servers, AMD racks, alongside healthy general server demand.

Company Description
Spun off from Wistron in March 2012, Wiwynn designs and manufactures cloud
infrastructure equipment for hyperscaler data centres. Prior to 2015, Wiwynn provided
storage servers and traditional servers. In 2015, Wiwynn began to shift its focus to

manufacturing full rack server for hyperscale data centre clients. Its key clients include US
Facebook (50-60% of total revenue), Microsoft (40-50%) and Amazon. Wiwynn is the
second-largest white-box server manufacturer in terms of shipments. It has production sites
in Mexico, the Czech Republic and China.
UBS EPS and Consensus EPS
The UBS EPS is an adjusted diluted EPS metric. It is calculated using the UBS analyst's
interpretation of earnings suitable for valuation purposes divided by the diluted number of

shares. This may differ to the way the consensus EPS metric has been calculated.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
Our price target is based on PE multiple methodology.
Key downside risks for Wiwynn include: 1) a slowdown in the US CSP capex cycle; 2) margin
compression due to intense competition; and 3) unfavourable FX movement.

asset. Investors could also lose their entire investment if the issuer becomes insolvent. UBS does not guarantee in any way the obligations or the financial condition of any

issuer or the accuracy of any financial information provided by any issuer. Structured investments are not traditional investments and investing in a structured investment is
not equivalent to investing directly in the underlying asset. Structured investments may have limited or no liquidity, and investors should be prepared to hold their investment
to maturity. The return of structured investments may be limited by a maximum gain, participation rate or other feature. Structured investments may include call features and,

if a structured investment is called early, investors would not earn any further return and may not be able to reinvest in similar investments with similar terms. Structured
investments include costs and fees which are generally embedded in the price of the investment. The tax treatment of a structured investment may be complex and may differ
from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

before investing in any securities.

### Page 3

Price Target Risks and Methodology - Quanta 
We are Neutral-rated on Quanta. Our 12-month target price of NT$299 is based on an 
10.7x 2027E P/E, which references PC/server peers’ EPS growth vs. P/E multiple 
correlation. We see EPS growth as a major factor for the stock’s performance.  
Key upside/downside risks include: 1) stronger-/weaker-than-expected PC market 
recovery; 2) faster-/slower-than-expected AI server ramp-up; and 3) 
stronger-/weaker-than-expected demand for general servers.

大量科技主要做PCB 機鑽與量測設備 ， 研究部維持強力買進投資建議 ，
係因 ： （1）總月產能已達 400 台並維持滿載 ， 預期今年出貨將超過1000
台，優於3 月法說展望；（2）TM 量測設備重要性與獨佔性不斷提升，
公司持續從 25 年 TM2 迭代至2H26 TM4 提升產品組合，預期拉貨比例
將從 8 台背鑽機對應 1 台 TM4 提升到 5：1，有望使公司市占率大幅
提升； （3）大量先進智慧在切入半導體大廠製程站點後，26-27 年也
將翻倍成長。綜上所述，預估26/27 年營收 97 與 137 億元上修到 125
與 229 億元（+146%/+83%YoY），稅後EPS 從 27 與 43 元上修到 28 與
70 元。研究部認為PCB 產業持續擴張，同時規格不斷升級。大量科技
位於客戶擴廠的風口浪尖，其量測技術與獨家產品成為公司提升市占
率與切入半導體的關鍵護城河，稼動率滿載的同時積極擴產。給予 27
年 22 倍 PE，目標價從 1220 元上修到 1540 元（2027 EPS*22PER）。

重點摘要： 
1. 公司簡介 
大量科技（3167）成立於 1980 年，總部位於桃園市八德區。
2004 年4 月興櫃，2013 年 10 月上市。主要提供 PCB 與半導體
設備，包含 PCB 標準鑽孔機、成型機與高階 CCD 背鑽機、CCD
成型機、TM 量測機，進行鑽孔定位、PCB 成型切割、鑽孔、塗
佈等；半導體設備包含 Metrology、AOI 與自動化設備即時量
測、檢測。台灣八德為總部，江蘇設有南京與漣水兩個工廠。
服務據點遍及中國、印度、東南亞及韓國、日本等地。主要客
戶為各大台系、中系 PCB 板廠， 競爭對手為德系 Schmoll（施
摩爾） 與中系大族數控。2025 年產品組合為 PCB 高階設備 
61%、低階設備 20% 與半導體 9%，25 年高低階出貨量約 4 : 
6。

2. 產品組合持續優化，2Q26 財報優於預期 
大量科技 2Q26 營收 28.6 億元 （+47%QoQ，+125%YoY） ，優於原
先預期 23.9 億元。毛利率 44.2%，優於原先預期 43.4%，顯
示高毛利產品佔比提升，產品組合持續優化。先前費用預估過
度樂觀，儘管費用從原先 2.73 億元調整至 4.97 億元（費用
率 17.4%），2Q26 稅後 EPS 仍達 6.10 元，優於原先預期。
2Q26 淨利率從 4 月 21% 一路月增至6 月達 33%， 稅後EPS 從單
月 1.55 元提升至 2.69 元。隨著訂單與出貨量持續墊加，公司
將逐月顯現營運槓桿帶來獲利大幅提升。

4. 供需缺口將逐漸擴大，26 年迎來機鑽長期結構性擴張循環 
AI 伺服器 PCB 正進入從需求量與價值同步提升的結構性擴張
循環。市場普遍預期 25-27 年 NV AI Server 機櫃出貨量將從
2.5 萬櫃提升至 8 萬櫃，成長逾 3 倍，CAGR+79%。產品主力由
GB300 逐步轉向 Vera Rubin 。此外，單一 AI 機櫃 PCB 面積與
層數也將持續增加，從25 年 GB 22-24 層持續提升至 27 年 26-
78 層，SemiAnalysis 估計，VR 每櫃高階 PCB 面積約較 GB 增加 
2.3 倍 ， 後續 Rubin Ultra 持續 朝 更 高 層 數 Midplane ／
Backplane 發展，每櫃高階 HLC PCB 數量、面積及板厚皆呈結
構性增加。帶動機鑽孔數增加外，板厚、板硬也將使得機鑽單
位時間上升。同時 SerDes 從 112G 向 224G 演進後，殘銅精度
要求持續提升，CCD 背鑽與 TM 量測的滲透率也將同步增加。

圖四、 背鑽需求倍數成長

資料來源：統一投顧整理

5. TM 量測機重要性持續上修成公司市占率提升關鍵 
公 司 近 年 推 出 內 層 深 度 量 測 設 備TM 系 列 （Inner Layer 
Thickness Metrology），解決 AI Server PCB 隨板層數、鑽
孔數及傳輸速率提升後，背鑽在殘銅精度要求提升的問題。
Rubin／224G 世代對殘銅精度要求由過去 ±3 mil 持續提升
至 ±2 mil 。TM 會先用探測棒逐片 360 度量測通孔內層銅層
實際深度，再將 Z 軸資料傳給背鑽進行加工。大量科技在量
測方面具有軟硬體技術護城河，目前同業尚無法效仿大量科技
的成熟度與良率，因此公司在未來世代產品極具有獨佔性。25
年首要推出以單軸 TM2 為主，1H26 為大平台單軸 TM3，2H26
後開始均為大平台四軸 TM4。 
公司 TM 量測機只能與公司高階背鑽機搭配使用，無法與同業
背鑽機兼容 ， 背鑽機有望透過TM 高獨佔性提升拉貨動能 。 過去
公司預期每 8 台背鑽機將搭配 1 台 TM 訂單，隨著 PCB 面積
與板層數成長恐面臨微翹曲問題，每孔的孔洞與深度差異化更
大 ， 加上板廠出現爆板等良率問題 ， 更加凸顯未來TM 量測的重
要性。目前拉貨比例已提高至約 1:5-1:6，預期精度要求將會
持續提高，若要提升良率與生產效率，TM 需求將有大幅成長空
間，公司更有機會藉 TM 的技術門檻反向提升高階背鑽市占
率，成為長期成長引擎。

7. HDI 滲透率提升，HLC 亦將同步增加 
近年 HDI 滲透率持續提升至目前約 18-20%，AI GPU／ASIC 的
I/O 數量、頻寬與封裝密度快速提升，使傳統機鑽無法滿足
Fine-pitch 與繞線密度需求，帶動Compute Board 由 4+N+4 逐
步升級至 7+N+7。HDI 具孔徑小、 繞線密度高、 訊號路徑短等特
性，不過目前在壓合良率與製程成本仍具挑戰，因此目前滲透
率仍有上限，且 UBB、Switch、Midplane 及 Backplane 仍需要
高層數 HLC、大孔徑 PTH、Power/Ground 與 Connector 互連。
且 Compute board 改為 HDI，中間核心層仍將由 20-30 層持續
往上成長，板子越厚，機鑽加工時間越長。因此，外層 HDI 階
數增加與內部 HLC 層數將同步增加而非互相取代，不影響機
鑽 TAM 的成長。

8. 未來若導入 PTFE 有望再提升機鑽單位需求 
AI Server 高速傳輸由 112G 往 224G、448G 演進後，PCB 傳
輸損耗成為系統瓶頸 ， 傳統 FR-4／高階 Low-loss CCL 的 Dk、
Df 與高頻穩定性面臨更高要求 ， 產業開始評估以PTFE 與既有
高階材料混壓，取代部分傳統 Epoxy／Hydrocarbon 樹脂介電
層，尤其集中在高速訊號層，降低介電損耗與訊號衰減。PTFE
優點為低 Dk、極低 Df、耐高頻與電氣特性穩定，適合 224G 
以上高速傳輸 ， 不過材料成本 、 壓合與表面處理難度較高 。PTFE 
本體較軟、容易變形，不同材料又可能增加刀具磨耗。大量科
技已測試多種材料方案，未來 M8/M9、混壓PTFE 等高速材料導
入後 ， 鑽孔機本身架構不需大幅改變 ， 但鑽針壽命 、 加工參數 、
板厚、翹曲與內層偏移均更加複雜，且 PTFE 質地柔軟易變形，
單位鑽孔時間恐變慢，反而提高量測與機鑽需求，導入反而對
機鑽產業前景正向。

9. 大量切入半導體量測，未來有望翻倍成長 
大量科技技術優勢在於高精度物理量測 、AI 視覺控制 ，22 年結
合公司既有高精度設備、運動控制、視覺檢測與系統整合能力
延伸至半導體設備，23-25 年隨先進封裝擴產而快速成長。產
品包含 Metrology、AOI 與自動化設備，應用於前段晶圓製造、
中段 CoW 與後段 oS。隨 CoWoS 封裝尺寸放大 ， 翹曲導致厚度 、
高度差與邊緣等量化控制的重要性提高，大量過往 TM 量測機
在 PCB 殘銅精度量測達業界之最，公司除了檢測是否缺陷外，
還能判斷缺陷、翹曲程度，成為公司切入半導體檢測量測的關
鍵。公司已切入CoWoS 多項站點，同時亦布局 SoIC、FOPLP／

綜上所述，原預期 26-27 年高階設備出貨約 1000-1500 台，
隨著財報中營收與在手訂單開出，加上供應鏈觀察可以發現，
26-27 年需求量將遠優於預期。因此研究部將26-27 年高階設
備出貨上修至 1400-2400 台。預估 26/27 年營收 97 與 137 億
元上修到 125 與 229 億元（+146%/+83%YoY），稅後EPS 從 27
與 43 元上修到 28 與 70 元。

矽格 (6257 TT)  Buy

AI 和矽光訂單貢獻將逐步增加，建議 Buy。  
投資建議 ： AI、 ASIC 、矽光子與高速運算是矽格 2026 年最明
確、也是最重要的成長引擎。受惠於客戶端龐大的需求，這三
大板塊的營收佔比已躍升至 20% 以上。其中， ASIC 與矽光子是
目前毛利率最高的產品線，加上 CP 佔比提升，產品組合改變，
有利毛利率向上。預估矽格 2026 年稅後 EPS 9.91 元。雖消費
性電子需求溫和，不過矽格積極開發新客戶、新產品以增加成
長動能。美系 CSP 持續增加 ASIC 量，帶動後段測試需求吃緊，
除美國外，矽格還有日本及歐美 ASIC 等新客戶，另原大客戶也
跨入 AI 晶片，公司配合增加資本支出，將帶動未來 AI 相關訂
單成長 。 由於測試產能吃緊(測試廠 80% 為滿載 ， 考慮換線時間)，
預期價格將續漲，加上新產能開出， 2026 年營收和毛利率有望
逐季向上，因此建議 Buy ，目標價為 304 元 (2027 年 PER24X) 。 
2Q26 稅後 EPS 2.52 元 ：矽格 2Q26 營收 58.81 億元，
QoQ+11.09% 。 2Q26 雖然部份客戶產品受到記憶體價格上漲影
響，對營收成長動能造成一定程度壓抑；惟受惠客戶在 AI 伺服
器、 ASIC 、AI Connectivity 、矽光子、網通晶片及記憶體等領域
需求持續擴增，加上公司擴產計畫穩步推進，先前追加資本支
出所採購之設備將陸續到位，並逐步挹注營收表現，使營收持
續保持一定動能。受惠稼動率維持高檔，使毛利率也上揚。矽
格 2Q26 稅後 EPS 2.52 元。  
2026 年資本支出提升至 88 億元 ：矽格董事會上修全年度資本
支出，由原先規劃的 59 億元大幅提高至 88 億元，增幅達 49%。
主要用於採購先進製程測試設備，以滿足 AI、 ASIC 及 HPC 等
強勁的市場需求。預計 2H26 湖口二廠將加入生產。因獲得客戶
訂單保證，將在 07/2026 開始貢獻營收，以矽光為主；規模較大
中興三廠亦提前於 4Q26 建置完畢，為中長期先進製程訂單提
供充裕的產能擴展空間，預計 1Q27 進入量產。折舊費用方面，
新設備 4Q25 陸續安裝， 2Q26 後，折舊費用將會逐季增加。

  矽格 ESG ：  
矽格體認企業永續經營運作與全球多元劇變之發展密不可分，因此我們建
立並持續發展各項符合國際倡議之永續經營管理策略，善盡企業社會責任，
共同保護我們所共享的地球環境。  
「落實公司治理」  
氣候相關財務揭露  (TCFD) 報告，揭露透過治理、策略、風險管理、指標與
目標，並於同年成立風險管理委員會展開氣候變遷調適及減緩管理行動，董
事會亦每季審查集團各子公司之溫室氣體推展進度及成效管理，邁向低碳
永續之倡議。  
「環境保護永續」  
矽格積極實施低碳策略之行動方案，落實節能、節水、減廢等相關作為邁進
永續封測，並積極佈局支持再生能源使用。  
「智慧創新管理」  
持續推動智慧製造工廠，落實運用智慧管理模式提升客戶滿意績效的最佳
化表現。自主研發機台因應不同客戶客製化需求產出所需，提供客戶多樣化
選擇和更具競爭力的解決方案優化複雜製程，以低碳產品之前瞻技術為永
續競爭力。  
「綠色營運供應」  
綠色營運供應落實管理，矽格不僅關心企業內部的環境管理及相關教育訓
練，同時也關注供應商管理，推動供應商共同承擔環境及社會責任。因此，
矽格建立供應商管理程序，確保企業永續發展落實執行與督導供應鏈。  
「建立友善職場」  
落實勞動人權策略提供多元溝通管道途徑，在符合法令、公平與合理性之前
提下，致力符合同仁期待與需求，提升全體同仁勞動權益，促使職場達到溝
通無障礙。  
「投入社會參與」  
投入社會參與落實企業社會責任議題是矽格集團持續並強化落實的永續發
展策略之一，不論是贊助醫學預防的臺大醫院之 「心臟血管基因研究計畫」 、
落實在地關懷世光教養院附設拙茁家園車輛贊助等 … 都是矽格依循永續理
念，秉持踏實精神與環境、社會共生共榮的態度在企業永續的道路上堅定前
行。

  投資評等係「首次」給予特定個股投資評等時，其前一日收盤價相較 3 個月

爾後的投資評等係依循「首次評等」，直到停止推薦。

首次評等時潛在報酬率不同。「中立」則無目標價。  
一旦我們給予特定個股「強力買進」 、 「買進」或「區間操作」之投資評等，

股價變化，直到停止推薦。  
停止推薦情境：

### Page 2

2

矽力杰為電源管理晶片大廠：矽力杰成立於 02/2008，為電源管理 IC 設計公司，
產品線包括 DC/DC 轉換晶片、電池充電管理晶片、過流保護晶片、靜電防護裝置
與 LED 背光驅動晶片、能源監控管理晶片等。矽力杰 2Q26 產品終端應用主要區
分為四大領域，包括消費電子(如平板電腦、STB 與 TV)36%、工業應用(如 LED 照
明、伺服器與安防設備等)35%、資訊產品(如筆電)9%與網路通訊(如路由器、手機
等)6%、 車載14%。 國際電源管理晶片設計同業與矽力杰產品類似者為TI、Maxim、
ON Semi 與 ADI，台系類似的參與廠商則包括致新、茂達等。 
3Q26 營收優於預期：矽力杰 08/2026 營收 24.16 億元(+2%MoM，+52%YoY)，
總計 07~08/2026 營收 47.7 億元，落於研究部原預估 3Q26 營收的 75%，優於
預期。矽力杰2H26 營運動能，若以各終端應用區分則：資料中心為最主要推升力
道 、 車載上升(新款晶片推出與市占率提升)、 消費電子上升(即便市場需求較為疲弱 ，
但因公司新款晶片推出，故反而仍能向上)、資通訊產品下滑(因記憶體報價上漲，
推高終端售價而影響消費力道)、 網通滑落 。 整體而言 ， 矽力杰法說時表示3Q26 營
收僅微幅上升，實屬偏為保守(畢竟 07/2026 開始漲價，又車載與資料中心動能依
舊較為強勢)，目前展望 4Q26 展望亦正向。只是公司仍認為 2026 年隨正負因子
交雜，毛利率較有變數(包括晶圓/封測成本上升、存貨依據庫齡政策而有損失或回
沖認列、 公司依據產品與客戶別而有不等的漲價措施、 第四代製程平台挹注與產品
結構變化等)，不過研究部認為隨 07/01 已開始進行漲價，理應能消弭部分製造成
本攀升的衝擊 ， 遂預估2H26 毛利率應能優於 2Q26 水準 。 研究部預估矽力杰3Q26
營收 71.2 億元(+18%QoQ，+49%YoY)，毛利率 48.21%，稅後獲利 10.16 億元
(-35%QoQ，+49%YoY)，稅後 EPS 2.6 元，並預估 4Q26 營收 75.13 億元
(+5.5%QoQ，+39%YoY)。 
2027 年樂觀以待 ， 資料中心與車載為成長主軸 ：矽力杰(1) 2027 年營收樂觀以待 ，
主要由資料中心/車載/工業推升整體動能 。(2) 資料中心(包括主板/企業級 SSD/光
模組)目前營收比重 15%~16%，2027 年預期>20%比重，公司資料中心三大項目
比重依序為光通訊>SSD>MB，其中光通訊與 SSD 個別均為 mid-to-high single 
digit，MB 比重較低。公司過往以 400G 以下為主，今年 400G/800G 均已導入，
隨市占率逐步提升，又未來若主板核心電源出貨，更將進一步推動資料中心業務規
模擴大。(3) 車載則來自公司車載晶片供應品項增加，每台車的可供應的內含價值
擴大，並且客戶群攀升，除中國品牌上量外，也進一步拓展海外市場。雖現階段車

 投資評價與建議 
隨著RISC-V需求持續提升，公司開案數同步增加，惟公司短期仍以授權費為
主，且轉向大型客戶使得案件認列時程拉⻑，營收波動也較大。 
 重點評論分析 
3Q26尚無客戶大型專案貢獻，推估營收季減約18%，4Q26將回復成⻑：來自
歐美車用客戶也開始貢獻授權金 ， 惟美系CSP客戶因大型專案墊高2Q26基期 ，
推估25Q3營收4.64億元，QoQ-18.1%，因人員裁撤，費用將明顯下滑，推估
約4.5億元，本業有望轉為正數，EPS 0.25元。展望4Q26，因季底通常為授權
金認列高峰，推估營收5.15億元，QoQ+11.5%，本業亦有望維持獲利。 
費用開始嚴控，有望自2H26起維持本業獲利態勢，2027年展望正向：隨著公
司轉向大型客戶專案與車用市場，因案件時程拉⻑和車用認證期較⻑，使得各
季的營收波動較大，展望未來，隨著歐美客戶車用產品開案完成，車用產品將
是主要成⻑動能，惟目前仍以授權費為主，雖消費性產品需求不佳，然在客戶
降低成本考量，以及網通產品為提升運算與資料傳輸的效能與彈性，如達發
(6526)已宣布擴大採用RISC-V ， 皆有助公司營運 ， 而費用自3Q26起開始嚴控 ，
本業有望開始維持獲利，2027年隨著案件數進⼀步增加，本業獲利將明顯提
升；整體而言，公司對於RISC-V未來發展趨勢仍樂觀看待。 
 投資風險 
先進製程等案件持續不如預期。

| 公司簡介  
晶心科為全球RISC-V CPU IP龍頭廠，市占率約30%：公司成立於2005年，早期專注自有架構V3，2016年開始轉
為RISC-V架構之CPU IP授權 ， 目前授權費占比約65%為主要營收貢獻 ， 權利金仍有待時間發酵 ， 其中授權費>90%
來自RISC-V ， 權利金則以V3占90%為主 ， 2018年開始收取RISC-V權利金 ， 占比約10% ， 產品線以32/64 bit為主，
員工人數約400人(短期若無營收顯著增⻑機會，公司會維持此規模)，其中研發人員約佔80%，先前北美約100多
人的團隊已裁撤，客戶數超過400家，採用公司IP出貨之SOC已突破170億顆，根據SHD 2024年行銷報告，晶心
科在RISC-V供應商市占率約30%，為全球第⼀大廠，產品應用涵蓋AI、消費性、IOT、網通等，AI占比>40%為最
大應用，消費性占比隨市況波動較大，占比由過往最大逐步降至低於20%，IOT占比約15%並持續朝20%邁進，車
用占比仍為個位數，但多為歐美客戶，未來成⻑性佳，占比將大於10%，出貨地區以台灣40%與美國30%為主，
中國地區因競爭性較大，未來將降低此處營運力道，比重已低於20%。 
相較於x86架構（Intel和AMD的處理器採用）為少數仍使用CISC（complex instruction set computer，複雜指
令集）設計，ARM、MIPS與RISC-V等架構皆採RISC（reduced instruction set computer，精簡指令集）設計，
ARM架構受惠低功耗優勢及完整生態系統，使得手持式裝置甚至更多應用大量採用，但其閉源架構及高額授權費
與權利金，也促使開源免費且可自由修改設計架構的RISC-V需求明顯提升，惟目前生態系統仍有待時間發展，晶
心科為RISC-V創始會員 ， 也是最大供應商 ， 其餘具代表性公司包含SiFive 、 平頭哥 、 芯來(芯原於2025/09/11 100%
收購)等。 
| 營運概況  
2Q26認列進度佳，惟組織調整造成持續虧損：受惠美系CSP廠AI產品貢獻授權金，2Q26營收5.66億元，創新高，
QoQ+73.5%，其中授權金3.8億元，創新高，顯示公司新開案情形良好，因公司裁撤美國部門仍需支付資遣費，
費用6.7億元，亦同創新高，然未來費用將明顯下降，因此本業持續虧損，EPS -1.34元，低於預期。 
3Q26尚無客戶大型專案貢獻，推估營收季減約18%，4Q26將回復成⻑：來自歐美車用客戶也開始貢獻授權金，
惟美系CSP客戶因大型專案墊高2Q26基期，推估25Q3營收4.64億元，QoQ-18.1%，因人員裁撤，費用將明顯下
滑，推估約4.5億元，本業有望轉為正數，EPS 0.25元。展望4Q26，因季底通常為授權金認列高峰，推估營收5.15
億元，QoQ+11.5%，本業亦有望維持獲利，推估EPS 0.9元。

降低成本考量，以及網通產品為提升運算與資料傳輸的效能與彈性，如達發(6526)已宣布擴大採用RISC-V，皆有
助公司營運，而費用自3Q26起開始嚴控，本業有望開始維持獲利，2027年隨著案件數進⼀步增加，本業獲利將明
顯提升；整體而言，公司對於RISC-V未來發展趨勢仍樂觀看待，中⻑期而言，SHD Group預估在MCU、AI加速器
與網通等應用推升下，全球RISC-V 晶片出貨將加速攀升，至2030年出貨量將達162億顆，晶心科將同步受惠。

⻑期產業趨勢正向，惟營運波動較大，仍有待成效展現，投資建議維持中立評等：隨著RISC-V需求持續提升，公
司開案數同步增加，惟公司近年成⻑性仍以授權費為主，權利金成⻑趨勢相對較緩，且轉向大型客戶與專案後，
案件認列時程拉⻑，營收波動也較大。

### Page 1

Mid-Qtr Update on Yield Expansion, Foundry Wins

Maintained  Buy  
 Target price $150

Raise TP to $150: Intel share price has underperformed since July, due to new share 
offerings (which we view as long -term constructive) and concerns over PC cuts at TSMC 
which were misleading. Based on our supply chain research, we believe its yields for server 
CPU (18A) and EMIB substrate were better than expected. That said, it is on track to expand 
the Foundry client base which will be from existing top-tier U.S. fabless to Terafab cooperation 
and HBM base die, which is likely in 2029 for 2 major ones. Meanwhile, CPU tailwinds, 
strengthened by GPT-6, continue. We fine  tune our EPS estimates by + 2%/+0% in 
2026E/2027E and lift TP from $136 to $150, now based on SOTP.  
CPU tailwinds on GPT-6, NVDA cooperation for head-node: We expect compute demand 
to continue scaling, with GPT-6’s agentic capabilities, which extends from coding to broader 
knowledge work such as financial modeling and scientific workflows, benefiting CPU demand. 
We reiterate our view that the global server CPU TAM to reach $211bn by 2030. For Intel, we 
believe its CWF will start in small volume in late -2026 with full production in 1Q27, yet, the 
major volume will be Diamond Rapids, supported by stronger SRAM/LPDDR5X and number 
of cores, likely in mid-2027. For NVDA, we still expect a potential cooperation in PC and now 
expect a likely x86 CPU adoption for head-node as a variant of Rosa Feynman platform.  
Foundry yields & projects: 1) Yields: Following our earlier view of  18A yields of ~80% in 
2Q26 for Pather Lake, we believe the larger sized server CPU, CWF, has been improved to 
~50% yields, vs. ~20% in June ; 2) Capacity: we reiterate our report of Big Lift on Foundry 
Capacity on June 8 of 40/60/80KPM and 0/6/24KPM for 18A/14A by end-2026/2027/2028. 3) 
Projects: Following our report of More Than Just Apple on Dec 1 (highlighted Apple, Nvidia, 
etc), we believe it is working on the Terafab project, likely providing lP licensing, factory build-
up, etc. 4) HBM base die: We expect it to be in 2029, likely for 2 major HBM suppliers. 
EMIB & substrate yields tracking ahead : We believe the market concerns over EMIB 
substrate yields  were based on outdated datapoints , while our supply chain research 
suggests development continues to advance, with tw o Japanese suppliers improving yields 
from 20–25% on initial testing vehicles to ~45% on the testing vehicles in Aug. This is on track 
to reach the following yield target of >50% in certified testing vehicles and ~55% in Jan. We 
reiterate our robust customer pipeline on $1.1bn/$7bn backend revenue in 2027E/2028E.  
Risks: 1) AI slowdown; 2) new product/node delay; 3) yield rates; 4) competition.

Valuation and Recommendation  
Maintain Buy with TP of $150 
We rate Intel (INT C US) Buy and set our TP at $ 150, which is based on : 1) 3. 5x our 202 8E BVPS 
estimate for Foundry business, a level we view as justified and is slightly higher than tier-2 makers due 
to Made in U.S. advantages; 2) 20x our 2028E EPS of its Design business, which is lower than the 
target multiple assigned to its peers’ such as AMD, as we believe its Design business is still losing 
shares in server and part of the earnings is to fund its Foundry segment. Overall , we project its ROE 
will recover to an above 10% level by 2028E amid the trend of Made in U.S.  
Intel’s P/B traded at an average of 1. 8x post pandemic when the new “IDM 2.0” and “5Y4N” strategy 
rolled out, though it didn’t really execute. Share price was volatile in the past few years due to events 
of: 1) multiple delays in leading technologies; 2) inferior financial performance of IFS; 3) mgmt. changes; 
4) weak position against TSMC. However, its P/B valuation moved up following the U.S. government’s 
stake purchase in Aug 2025. We expect the upward trend to continue, and our target price is at the high 
end of its cycle valuation, as we believe the New CEO Li p-Bu Tan’s initiatives with financial discipline 
and process technology development to remake Intel will enhance the company’s position in the 
industry. We believe the critical factors to watch will be Intel’s progress of 18A and 14A.

ab 16 June 2026
Global Research

APAC Focus:  How China's AI models compete
on cost efficiency
In the global AI race, model intelligence is key to assessing competitiveness and
commercialisation. However, as AI adoption shifts  to scaled deployment, we expect
cost efficiency to become increasingly important. Through targeted R&D,
architectural innovations, engineering optimisation and open-source collaboration,
we believe China's companies are rapidly closing the performance gap with global

leaders at markedly lower costs, making them well positioned to gain share in the
sizeable, expanding global AI TAM. We highlight  MiniMax, Zhipu, Alibaba,
Tencent and Baidu under our coverage as major companies in this theme,
together with private companies DeepSeek, Kimi, ByteDance and StepFun.
Assessing the cost leadership of China's AI models
We estimate the training costs for China's models (using MiniMax and Zhipu as
examples)  are less than 10% of those of global leaders such as OpenAI and Anthropic,

while the average API price of major China models is below 20% of comparable global
peers. However, China's frontier models are closing the capability gap with rapid
iteration and improving intelligence, gaining global traction in token usage while
preserving healthy gross margins.
Structural and sustainable efficiency gains in model training and inference
Supported by our technical analysis, we believe this reflects Chinese models' structural
advantages in model training and inferences. In training, China's model providers use

multiple approaches to reduce workload (via smaller parameters and sparse attention)
and improve GPU throughput, helped by targeted R&D and open-source ecosystems. In
inference, key innovations span model architecture (e.g., MoE, attention mechanism,
KV cache and lower precision), engineering optimisation (e.g.,  P/D separation, batching
and scheduling) and infrastructure (incl. domestic chip adaptation).
Reshaping global AI competition through superior cost-performance

We expect the global AI market to burgeon, with long-term TAM potentially surpassing
US$10trn, and see considerable scope for China's models to gain global market share.
As AI adoption moves from experimentation to scaled deployment,  companies are
shifting from maximising AI token usage (i.e., “token maxxing”) towards more ROI-
driven resource allocation. In our view, this shift should improve market recognition of
Chinese models' cost-performance advantages. We expect the global model market to

Q: Can China's AI models continue to close the performance gap at lower R&D costs?
Likely. We observe a narrowing gap in model intelligence between China's providers and global
leaders, yet R&D spending at China's AI labs remains considerably lower than those of US peers.

While distillation improves efficiency in model development, we believe China's model providers
adopt multiple approaches to reduce workloads (such as smaller parameters and sparse attention)
and improve GPU throughput, supported by targeted R&D and open-source ecosystems.
Q: Can China's models keep prices competitive for API services while  maintaining
reasonable gross margins?
Likely. We believe Chinese AI models' competitive API prices are not driven by high subsidies or a loss-

leading strategy, but by structural advantages in inference efficiency. We note key technological
innovations across: 1) model architecture such as mixture of experts (MoE), attention mechanisms,
KV cache and lower precision; 2) engineering optimisation, including P/D separation, batching and
scheduling; and 3) infrastructure, such as domestic chip adaptation. Despite prices at under 20% of
those of comparable US peers, API gross margins for China's AI models are around 20-40%, with

upside potential  if prices improve with model performance or additional gains in inference efficiency.
Q: How will China's AI models reshape the global model competitive landscape?
We view competition as a secondary concern in light of the rapidly expanding global AI TAM, which
we estimate could surpass US$10trn. As model supply is concentrated in the US and China, we
believe China's model providers should have meaningful opportunities for global expansion. As AI

adoption scales, we also expect demand to become increasingly tiered. While frontier models may
retain pricing premiums for complex, high-value tasks, cost-performance models could see broader
adoption in high-volume, ROI-sensitive workloads, creating global share-gain opportunities for
China's AI models in the longer term.
As AI adoption moves from experimentation to scaled deployment, we believe cost efficiency is likely
to become a key competitive factor alongside model intelligence. Based on our detailed technical

analysis, we believe China's AI model providers demonstrate structural and sustainable advantages in
training and inference efficiency, which make them well positioned to gain share in the large,
expanding global AI TAM, in our view. We highlight MiniMax, Zhipu, Alibaba and Tencent under our
coverage as major companies in this theme, together with private companies DeepSeek, Kimi,
ByteDance and StepFun.
1) China's frontier models have reached around 90% of the intelligence level of leading US models,

improving from around 60% in 2023, according to Artificial Analysis. 2) Total R&D costs of China's
listed AI model developers Zhipu/MiniMax amounted to US$0.5bn/US$0.3bn in 2025. This is around
one-tenth of Anthropic's R&D spending, and even lower relative to  OpenAI. 3) API pricing for China's
model  is significantly lower than those of US peers. Overall, we estimate API prices for China's
frontier models averages below 20% of comparable  US peers with similar  intelligence. 4) MiniMax's

M2.7 has gross margins of over 40%, broadly in line with Anthropic (roughly 40% in 2025, mainly
API and B2B-driven), and also comparable to  OpenAI's 40%/33% gross margin in 2024/25, which
benefits from a larger revenue contribution from consumer-facing, subscription-based services. Our
channel checks indicate API gross margins for China's major models are roughly in the 20-40%
range.
We believe investors do not fully appreciate or have strong conviction in Chinese AI labs' cost

leadership, and instead expect materially higher R&D investments and widening losses to support
model training and rising token demand. Investors seem also concerned that model offerings will
become commoditised over time, leading to intense price competition and potentially unsustainable
business models for China's AI model providers.

Figure 2: Glossary of key AI model concepts
Category Concept Explanation
Token The basic unit of text processed by a model. One token may correspond to a Chinese character or part of an
English word.
Parameters The internal weights of a model. More parameters usually indicate larger model capacity, but also higher
training and inference cost.
Context window The maximum amount of text / tokens a model can process in one request. A longer context window

supports longer documents and agentic tasks.
Long-horizon task A complex task that requires many steps, tool calls or extended context, such as AI coding, debugging or
project planning.
AI agent An AI system that can plan, use tools and take actions to complete tasks, rather than only responding in a
chatbot format.
Tool use / function calling The ability of a model to call external tools, APIs, databases or software functions to retrieve information or

execute actions.
MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) A model architecture where only a subset of parameters is activated for each token, reducing compute
requirements.
Sparse attention A design that allows the model to focus on the most relevant parts of the context rather than every token.
Training / inference precision The numerical format used in model computation, such as FP16, BF16 and FP8. Lower precision can reduce
compute and memory cost while maintaining model quality.

Quantization Reducing the numerical precision of model weights or computation to lower memory usage and inference
cost, often with limited impact on model quality.
Prefill The stage where the model reads and processes the input prompt before generating any output.
Decode The stage where the model generates output tokens one by one.
KV cache A stored representation of previously processed tokens that avoids recomputing the full context during
inference.

Prompt caching / cached input Previously processed input tokens that can be reused and charged at a lower cached-input price, instead of
being recomputed and charged as full input.
MFU (Model FLOPs Utilisation) A measure of how effectively a GPU’s theoretical compute capacity is utilised during model training or
inference.
Batching Grouping multiple requests together so GPUs can process them more efficiently.
Scheduling The system-level process of assigning requests to GPUs and managing task execution to improve utilisation

and latency.
Prefill-Decode separation Separating prefill and decode workloads onto different GPU resources to improve utilisation and reduce
latency.
TPS (tokens per second) The speed at which a model generates output tokens. Higher TPS means faster response generation.
TTFT (time to first token) The time between submitting a request and receiving the first output token. Lower TTFT improves perceived
latency.
GPU-hour One GPU running for one hour. It is a common unit for measuring training or inference compute cost.

Model router A system that selects the most suitable model for each task based on quality, cost, latency, reliability or
other routing rules.
AI gateway A unified access layer for multiple models / providers, often handling model routing, API management,
monitoring, security and cost control.
API pricing The price charged for model usage, usually based on tokens. Pricing is commonly split into uncached input
tokens, cached input tokens and output tokens.

Token plan A prepaid or subscription-style model usage package, often with a fixed monthly fee and token quota /
allowance.
MaaS (Model-as-a-Service) A business model where customers access models through APIs or cloud platforms and pay based on
usage.

China's AI labs are narrowing the performance gap at notably lower R&D
spending than US peers. Total R&D costs of listed Chinese AI model developers Zhipu/
MiniMax were US$0.5bn/US$0.3bn in 2025. This represents only around one-tenth of
Anthropic's R&D spending, and even less relative to  OpenAI, even when considering

suggests China’s  progress reflects a catch-up in  capability as well as significantly more

Distillation helps, but does not fully explain Chinese companies' efficient model

development.  We view model distillation as a teacher-student process, in which a
'student' model (often with fewer parameters) learns to mimic the outputs or behaviour
of a stronger 'teacher' model. Based on our channel checks with industry experts,
distillation can improve model capability with shorter training time and lower compute
costs, but its effectiveness is more visible in tasks with verifiable outcomes, repeatable
processes or easily imitable patterns. In contrast, distillation is less effective for

capabilities that are less verifiable, rely on complex multi-step processes or depend on
underlying architecture and system-level engineering ( Figure 7D is t illa t io n  h e lp s  in  v e r if ia b le  t a s k s  b u t  g e n e r a lly  h a s  lim it a t io n s  in  f r o n t ie r  c a p a b ilit ie s ). We believe  China's
progress in frontier models suggests capability gains beyond distillation alone. For
instance, Zhipu has demonstrated strong long-horizon reasoning, while MiniMax

models feature advanced multimodal capabilities.

Demystifying  China AI labs' R&D efficiency
China's model labs follow a more focused R&D strategy
In terms of R&D spending allocation, we observe differing strategic focus
between the US and China.  For US frontier labs, we see a larger share of R&D
spending being used for experimentation and path exploration , reflecting a stronger
emphasis on pushing the upper limits of model intelligence, supported by greater

compute resources. These experiments may span pre-training (non-Transformer
architecture for example), data (such as data curation and synthetic-data recipes), and
post-training stages (including  reinforcement learning from human feedback [RLHF] and
reinforcement learning-based reasoning and alignment). Taking OpenAI as an example,
Epoch AI data suggests that around 90% of the R&D compute budget is spent on
experimentation, with only about 10% used for final model training.

which could create meaningful cost-saving potential by reducing the trial-and-error
process. We think China’s different strategic choices versus the US are mainly driven by
two factors.

### Page 8

China Internet Sector 16 June 2026 ab 8
1. More constrained compute resources. China's labs appear to allocate a smaller
proportion of resources to broad experimentation, focusing instead on formal model
training, targeted capability improvements, and architecture and engineering
optimisation.
2. Open-source ecosystem helps spread experimentation costs across China's AI
labs. While individual labs in China tend to follow a more focused R&D path, the

broader open-source ecosystem allows technical learnings to diffuse across companies.
This means not every lab needs to independently repeat the same broad set of
experiments as closed-source US peers. Instead, once one lab validates an architecture,
training recipe or optimisation method, others can learn from it and build on top of it
(see examples below). In our view, this creates collective R&D leverage and lowers the
marginal cost of capability improvement for China's labs.

 Kimi K2 and GLM-5 have adopted MLA-like latent attention design following
DeepSeek’s earlier validation;
 Zhipu has adopted elements inspired by DeepSeek’s sparse attention mechanism;
 DeepSeek V4 has incorporated techniques related to Moonshot AI and Kimi’s
Muon optimiser;
 Qwen3 and Zhipu GLM-4.5 have implemented GRPO-style RL recipes following
DeepSeek.

Technological innovation to reduce training workload and improve

compute utilisation
Within R&D  spend, we analyse the largest cost component –  model training
compute costs. We estimate model training compute costs could account for 65-75%
of total R&D expenses for China's leading AI labs such as MiniMax and Zhipu. We think
model training compute costs can be interpreted as a function of the following key
factors, and we have  observed that China's AI labs are optimising several of these
factors.
 Total training workload, which is broadly determined by model size (namely the

number of parameters), and training token volume (generally related to dataset
size and attention mechanism);
 Effective GPU capacity, which depends on the GPU's peak performance and
actual utilisation during training, commonly measured by Model FLOPs Utilisation
(MFU). The model training workload is  divided by effective computing capacity per
GPU hour to derive the total GPU hours required.
 Cost per GPU hour , which is affected by utility costs and hardware efficiency

(such as  GPU).  Model training compute costs can be estimated by multiplying total
GPU hours required by the cost per GPU hour.

1. Lower training computational  workload from smaller parameters

and sparse attention
Smaller parameters help reduce model training workload but may also partly
explain  the performance gap. China's frontier models remain smaller than their US
counterparts on parameter scale. Total parameters for China's leading models are still
below 2trn (for example DeepSeek V4 at 1.6trn and Kimi K2.6 at around 1trn). For US
models, official data is limited due to their closed-source architectures, but academic
papers estimate leading models such as Claude Opus 4.6/ChatGPT 5.5 have scaled to

around 10trn/5trn parameters. That said, while smaller model size reduces training
workload for China's labs, it may also partly contribute to the capability gap versus US
frontier models, in our view.
Reduced training volume (in terms of effective token-interaction workload)
through sparse-attention architectures.  In Transformer models, attention
determines how each token incorporates information from other tokens in the
sequence. Full attention requires every token to interact with every other token, making

compute scale quadratically with context length. Sparse attention reduces this burden
by limiting attention to a subset of relevant tokens, thereby lowering effective token-to-
token interactions in long-context training and inference. Given more constrained
compute-resource availability, our channel checks of industry experts indicate China's AI
labs are putting more effort into sparse-attention designs to reduce compute
consumption. In comparison, US peers may place greater emphasis on model quality

(such as multi-step reasoning), where full attention remains a more robust but compute-
intensive design choice. For instance, DeepSeek V3.2 uses DeepSeek Sparse Attention
(DSA) to reduce the workload, while DeepSeek V4 adds context compression before the
sparse design based on V3.2 to improve long-context efficiency.

2. Increasing GPU throughput by adopting lower compute precision;

multiple approaches to improve MFU
As discussed in our training cost framework, in addition to reducing total compute
workload on the numerator side, AI labs can also lower total training costs by enlarging
the denominator, that is by increasing the effective computing capacity per GPU hour.
We see China's labs placing greater emphasis on lower compute precision.
Under the same GPU, lower precision can significantly increase throughput, as fewer
bits are used per value, enabling more calculations per unit time while reducing memory

usage and data movement. Taking the Nvidia B200 as an example, moving from BF16/
FP16 to FP8 can roughly double theoretical GPU throughput. While large-scale model
training has historically relied on BF16/FP16 mixed precision, we see China's AI labs
pushing the frontier of lower-precision training. Examples include DeepSeek-V3's FP8
mixed-precision training framework and DeepSeek V4's FP4 quantisation-aware training
for select model components. Meanwhile, Baidu's ERNIE 4.5 and 5.0 adopt FP8 mixed-

precision training, while Alibaba's Qwen3.5 introduces a native FP8 pipeline and FP8
end-to-end training techniques.
Multiple approaches to improve MFU.   China's AI labs are establishing dedicated AI
infrastructure teams to optimise compute resource utilisation. For instance, with its end-
to-end infrastructure team, MiniMax has achieved more than 75% MFU, a key indicator
of computational efficiency for model inference activities, higher than the industry

average of 40-50%. Specifically, MiniMax has implemented:
 Unified training and inference computing , with an intelligent scheduling
system that dynamically allocates computing resources between training and
inference tasks, maximising cluster utilisation without compromising
performance.
 Cross-cluster load balancing , which enables flexible resource distribution,
lowers latency and enhances reliability and disaster recovery.

3. Lower unit GPU-hour costs supported by utility efficiency
We note that China appears to have a relative advantage in GPU rental prices
versus the US for comparable GPUs. Taking Nvidia H100 rental prices as an example,
the average US price is about US$1.99-3.99/GPU-hour, while it is about 40% lower for
China, at about US$1.3-2.1/GPU-hour (Rmb9-15/GPU-hour). We believe lower utility

costs (typically a low-to-mid-teen percentage of data-centre total cost of ownership, or
TCO, according to SemiAnalysis), especially for electricity, could partly explain this gap,
although GPU rental prices are also affected by hardware amortisation, utilisation,
contract terms and providers' margins. In the US, we estimate the average electricity
price in key datacentre states such as Illinois and Georgia is about 7.9 cents/kWh, while
comparable regions in China average around 4.4 cents/kWh, or roughly 44% lower.

Similar to the high efficiency in model training, we see multiple inference-side
levers for China's model providers to optimise costs, supporting lower prices while
protecting margins. Specifically, we break down Chinese models’ inference efficiency

into three layers:
 Model architecture optimisation: Beyond smaller model sizes, China's labs are
adopting more sparse MoE architectures to reduce active compute. KV-cache
compression, built on sparse-attention designs, can further lower memory-related
costs, which we see as the largest inference cost component, while lower-
precision computation is also more widely used at the inference stage;
 Serving and engineering optimisation : Inference workloads are more

fragmented, real-time and heterogeneous than training, creating more room for
serving-layer optimisation such as P/D separation, batching and dynamic
scheduling, which can improve GPU utilisation and serving throughput;
 Resource and hardware optimisation : Similar to training, inference benefits
from China's energy-cost advantage, while domestic compute adoption appears
to be moving faster at the inference stage given workloads are more modular and

easier to optimise for specific models and use cases, in our view.
